answer.generated: A virtual memory management system consists of several key components including the page table, page replacement algorithm, and the page cache. The page table maps virtual addresses to physical addresses, facilitating efficient memory management by allowing processes to access their virtual address space independently. The page replacement algorithm works in conjunction with the page table to decide which pages to evict from main memory when they are replaced by new pages, aiming to minimize the number of page faults and thus enhance performance. The page cache further optimizes this process by temporarily storing frequently accessed pages, reducing the need for disk I/O operations and improving overall system efficiency.
